from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Big Picture: How AI Dreams", [

            "This process bridges language and pixels.",
            "CLIP connects text to image meanings.",

            "These models learn by iterative refinement."
        ])
        
        # Animations

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00BFFF")
        self.play(central_node.animate.scale(1.5).set_opacity(0.5), run_time=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF6347")
        features = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#00BFFF") for _ in range(4)])
        self.place_at_grid(features[0], 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(features[1], 'B4')
        self.place_at_grid(features[2], 'D2')
        self.place_at_grid(features[3], 'D4')
        self.play(FadeIn(features))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#32CD32")

        self.play(Create(connections))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF00FF")
        final_layer = Circle(color="#FF00FF", radius=0.4).move_to(self.grid['C3'])
        self.play(Flash(final_layer, color="#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(ThreeDScene, TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: High-Dimensional Spaces", [
            "Images exist in high-dimensional space.",
            "Each pixel contributes to a vector.",
            "Embeddings map features to coordinates."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw 2D grid representing base space
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 5, 1], y_range=[0, 5, 1], axis_config={"color": "#808080"}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#808080")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Add vector arrow representing a data point
        vector = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(3, 4), buff=0, color="#FF4500")
        dot = Dot(axes.c2p(3, 4), color="#FF4500")
        self.play(Create(vector), Create(dot))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")

        # Expand to 3D space with subtle rotation
        axes_3d = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[0, 5, 1], y_range=[0, 5, 1], z_range=[0, 5, 1], axis_config={"color": "#808080"}).scale(0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(axes_3d, 'C3')
        self.set_camera_orientation(phi=75 * DEGREES, theta=-45 * DEGREES)
        self.play(FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(vector), FadeOut(dot), Create(axes_3d))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Demonstrate vector projection
        vec_3d = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=axes_3d.c2p(3, 4, 3), color="#32CD32")
        self.play(Create(vec_3d))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#32CD32")
        
        # Highlight distance metric
        dot_a = Dot(axes_3d.c2p(3, 4, 3), color="#FF69B4")
        dot_b = Dot(axes_3d.c2p(1, 1, 1), color="#FF69B4")
        line_dist = Line3D(start=dot_a.get_center(), end=dot_b.get_center(), color="#FF69B4")
        self.play(Create(dot_a), Create(dot_b), Create(line_dist))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "CLIP aligns text and image vectors.", 
            "Similar items point the same way.", 
            "It measures proximity using cosine similarity.", 
            "This bridge maps language to vision.", 
            "AI interprets your prompt through CLIP."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("CLIP: The Bridge Between Text and Vision", lecture_lines)
        
        # Objects
        text_obj = Square(side_length=1, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        image_obj = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        vec_t = Dot(color="#FFFFFF")
        vec_i = Dot(color="#00FFFF")
        dist_line = Line(start=vec_t.get_center(), end=vec_i.get_center(), color="#FFFF00")
        sim_matrix = Rectangle(width=2, height=2, color="#ADFF2F", fill_opacity=0.3)
        concept_match = VGroup(Dot(color="#FF00FF"), Dot(color="#FF00FF")).arrange(RIGHT)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(text_obj, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(image_obj, 'B5')
        self.play(Create(text_obj), Create(image_obj))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(vec_t, 'D2')
        self.place_at_grid(vec_i, 'D5')
        self.play(FadeIn(vec_t), FadeIn(vec_i))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        dist_line.add_updater(lambda m: m.put_start_and_end_on(vec_t.get_center(), vec_i.get_center()))
        self.play(Create(dist_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#ADFF2F"))
        self.place_in_area(sim_matrix, 'E1', 'F6')
        self.play(FadeIn(sim_matrix))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.place_at_grid(concept_match, 'A3')
        self.play(FadeIn(concept_match))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Diffusion Models: The Mathematical Sculptor", [

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Text embeddings guide the denoising.", "They act as a semantic magnet.", "Pixels align with requested descriptions."]
        self.setup_layout("Guiding the Process: The Mathematics of Condition", lecture_lines)
        
        # --- Visualization elements ---
        # 1. Noise cloud
        noise_cloud = VGroup(*[Dot(self.grid["C3"] + np.random.randn(3)*0.5, color="#444444") for _ in range(50)])
        
        # 2. Prompt vector
        prompt_vec = Vector(RIGHT * 1.5, color="#FF69B4").move_to(self.grid["A4"])
        prompt_label = Text("Prompt Vector", font_size=18, color="#FF69B4").next_to(prompt_vec, UP, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display noise cloud #444444 and prompt vector #FF69B4
        self.play(FadeIn(noise_cloud), Create(prompt_vec), Write(prompt_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#444444")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate prompt influencing reverse diffusion trajectory #00BFFF
        influence_arrow = CurvedArrow(self.grid["A4"], self.grid["D3"], color="#00BFFF", angle=-TAU/8)
        self.play(Create(influence_arrow))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00BFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show step-by-step guidance #FFD700 adjusting image generation
        self.play(noise_cloud.animate.set_color("#FFD700"), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Text-to-Image AI: Diffusion, CLIP, and the Math Behind It
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic background in linear algebra and probability

sections.title: The Big Picture: How AI Dreams
sections.content: An overview of the Text-to-Image pipeline: How we map linguistic concepts (CLIP) to visual pixels (Diffusion).
sections.example: Inputting 'A robotic cat playing a violin' and seeing it transform from noise to a sharp, vivid image.

sections.title: Prerequisites: High-Dimensional Spaces
sections.content: Visualizing images as points in a massive vector space. Briefly introduce the concept of 'Embedding'—translating a cat's features into numerical coordinates.
sections.example: Imagine a 3D coordinate system where 'furriness' is the X-axis and 'whiskers' is the Y-axis; a cat sits at (0.8, 0.9).

sections.title: CLIP: The Bridge Between Text and Vision
sections.content: Explain Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) as a cross-modal translator that aligns text and image vectors using cosine similarity.
sections.example: If the text 'fluffy dog' and a photo of a puppy point in the same direction in vector space, the AI knows they match.

sections.title: Diffusion Models: The Mathematical Sculptor
sections.content: The forward process (adding Gaussian noise until the image is pure static) and the reverse process (the Neural Network learning to predict and remove noise).
sections.example: Visualizing a marble statue covered in snow (noise) and the AI 'chiseling' away the noise step-by-step to reveal the statue beneath.

sections.title: Guiding the Process: The Mathematics of Condition
sections.content: Explain how the text embedding (from CLIP) acts as a 'magnet' during the reverse diffusion process, steering the noisy pixels toward the desired outcome.
sections.example: Using the 'robotic cat' embedding to pull pixels into the shape of metal ears and strings during the denoising steps.
